externalReview.formalConditions: Verified current 2026–2027 regulatory framework from the actual official 32-page OER (effective 1 September 2026), visually compared with extracted text. Articles 3.4–3.6, pages 12–16: eight 15-EC blocks in years 1–2, 25-EC free choice, 15-EC Choices and Dilemmas and 20-EC graduation = 180 unique EC; K/AVV/integration submodules are children and not additional credits. PPO is pass/fail without separate EC in this framework. Article 4.1 and 8.1 require positive first-year BSA for later-year blocks; normally 60 EC plus PPO with article 3.5 first-year compensation (one 5.0–5.4 compensated by another module at least 6.0). No between-module compensation in years 2–3. Graduation entry requires all B1/B2 components and a timely secured placement; the three GW310/GW311/GW312 codes represent alternative start trajectories for one 20-EC project, not cumulative projects. Free choice permits approved minors/electives/exchange/international placement under article 3.6; outside LDE universities needs examination-board permission requested at least eight weeks in advance; exchange needs board-approved non-overlapping on-campus formally assessed courses, at least half B2 level, minimum 25 EC; international placements of 10/15 EC need coordinator approval. Required mentoring/coaching/intervision and stated participation requirements are non-credit obligations. Honours is extracurricular. Appendix 1, page 31, explicitly starts the redesigned curriculum in 2027–2028: free choice changes from 25 to 30 EC, graduation from 20 to 30 EC and Block 9 from 15 to zero. The public programme page’s 30 EC therefore is not imported into the retained 2026–2027 framework. This is a year-specific regulatory snapshot, not a guarantee that a new entrant will retain unchanged rules throughout three future years. No visible/hidden text disagreement was found on the inspected current and future tables.

alignmentReview.reason: Both directly examine how biological, psychological and social factors shape health, illness and patient experience. Erasmus also integrates legal patient status and questions about health knowledge; UCR concentrates on health psychology.
Both study change across the lifecourse and older age. UCR supplies developmental psychology; Erasmus integrates care needs, ageing and social/organisational/government responses.
Health psychology and youth resilience inform service-user needs, but do not directly deliver the block’s youth-service policy, legal responsibilities, waiting lists and stakeholder project.

Both examine ethical problems raised by data and technology in care. UCR explicitly discusses clinical/therapeutic confidentiality, trust and responsibility in AI; Erasmus addresses a broader set of healthcare dilemmas.
General law and political science do not deliver the Dutch healthcare system’s institutions, financing arrangements and healthcare-specific legal framework.

Both use economic analysis of consumer/provider behaviour, market structures and intervention. UCR teaches general microeconomics; Erasmus specifically studies insurer/provider and insurance markets and their legal rules.

Both directly examine organisational structures, culture, leadership, groups and coordination. UCR supplies general organisational behaviour, while Erasmus integrates healthcare organisations, financial/logistical data and observation.

AI ethics covers an identifiable ethical part of health technology, but is more strongly aligned to Choices and Dilemmas. No included course establishes the complete healthcare innovation/business-case/implementation project.
No scheduled course directly teaches the integrated measurement, improvement, professional regulation and quality governance of healthcare.

The current OER establishes 25 EC of approved minor/elective, exchange or international-placement choice. This has no fixed subject to align; UCR scheduled courses are not presented as a guaranteed approved choice package.

The compulsory 20-EC placement-based independent research/fieldwork project is not delivered by the scheduled research-synthesis seminar. Optional independent research is displayed separately outside the UCR 180 EC; it does not fulfil the required external placement.
